Comments: This well was inspected as part of a water supply complaint investigation involving a private water supply (CTS#379698). ¿¿ This well is located approximately 700’ east of the complainants water well. ¿¿ The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, corrosion, and possible failures. ¿¿ All valves were open, and the well is currently equipped for production.¿¿ ¿¿ No check valve was in place on the production line. ¿¿ The Well Records were reviewed to assist in the investigation.¿¿¿¿ ¿¿ Production and Mechanical Integrity Assessment Reports were reviewed and are not current.¿¿ The last reports submitted for mechanical integrity assessment was reporting year 2019. Violation ID: 8165817
Permit API: 125-23126
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: West Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/15/2023
Comments: On 11/15/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Cowden 55 well. On 08/23/2023, a routine partial inspection was conducted (IR 3606258).On 08/23/2023, the tank onsite displayed oil which looked as thought it was dripping down the side fro the top. The oil was on a small section of gravel. A smaller section of oil was on another side of the tank. The operator was notified the day of observation. There were no violations issued on 08/23/2023 due to size of area impacted. During inspection on 11/15/2023, for following was observed: The site appeared remediated regarding the oil from the top of the tank; the operator removed the impacted gravel and placed it in a bucket marked with 08/24/2023. The bucket remianed onsite; I recommend that this is removed and disposed of a an approproate waste facility (Photos 1-4). It also looked as thought the operator had wiped the side of the tank off. During the followup, a conductivity test was performed underneath the lower valve on the tank, which displayed iron stained gravel. Conductivity readings within the iron stained gravel, under the valve, yielded elevated results (Photos 5-7).During the initial inspection, a gas odor was noticed near the wellhead and I informed the operator. They informed operation's to inspect. They informed me that the grey apparatus on the well (Photo 8) was part of the landowner's hookup. When the operator followed up, their gas meter did not detect any gas. During the 11/15/23 follow up, the odor was noticed again to which I informed the operator. They followed up the same day and mentioned that the heater on the landowner's setup was functioning properly and may be bleeding; they recommendded a pressure test be performed. I contacted the landowner to inform them of what Diversified (operator) informed me of - they also contacted the landowner. I contacted the landowner about my conversation with the operator and recommended that the setup receives maintenance. The operator informed me that they thought the odor contained mercaptan and may be coming from a Columbia gas line nearby. Below the wellsite is a Williams station that the gas flows to. Regarding the elevated conductivity observed onsite below the valve of the production tank, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b)

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/01/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 958100
Permit API: 015-23674
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/06/2022
Comments: This inspection is to follow up on violations cited February 11, 2022 (inspection 3320334) after getting lab results for a liquid sample collected from the pad surface on February 1, 2022 (inspection 3315684). Today pooled liquid on top of the north slope has electrical conductivity (EC) of 4.0 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. Vegetation appears stressed on the slope below that EC reading. I spoke with Ashley Knox (CHK) on site and showed her the areas on the north and east slopes where the vegetation is sparse and appears stressed. Knox said Creston will likely sample soil to delineate any contamination.Vegetation, straw and rock stabilize soil of the site. Some of the vegetation is sparse. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation during this inspection. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact; I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies today. Workers are removing 8.93 mS/cm liquid from the wheelie trailer liner (photo). I did not see any pooled liquid on the pad surface.A wireline is preparing the new Marcellus wells here for hydraulic fracturing.Violations for a liquid release of unknown quantity cited to the 015-23674 permit on February 11, 2022 (inspection 3320334) remain outstanding. The DEP requests an update on the status of remediation at this site.Air temp 70JLP

Inspection Date: 10/03/2024
Comments: On 10/3/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a followup inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection was to assess areas on the pad that had water with elevated levels of conductivity as witnessed on 10/2/2024, inspection record 3844333.When I arrived at the site, I discussed with Mark McCormick that I would be field testing water puddles on the pad surface and water in the MRC basin on the north side of the pad. If the results did have elevated readings, I would be collecting water samples.I was unaccompanied during this inspection. Two water puddles field tested at 19.99 mS conductance, one 6' x 1.5' x 3" deep and one 10' x 3' x 2" deep; both near the center of the north perimeter berm outfall. The water puddles were located under the freshwater and under the mixed freshwater/brine water pipelines. The puddles each had a multi-colored thin crusty film on the surface that fractured when disturbed. I collected water sample 9551-142 from the 6' x 1.5' x 3" deep puddle.I witnessed a water/muddy area in the MRC basin, pictures 8, 9 and 10, coming from the rock outfall from the center of the north side of the pad. Water in this area field tested at 16.92 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551143 from the outfall entry point into the MRC basin.Water in the MRC basin field tested at 1.595 mS conductance near the northeast MRC basin discharge. I collected sample 9551-144 from the MRC basin near the northeast discharge.The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the MRC basin.The DEP recommends the following:1. Remove the elevated conductance water puddles from the pad surface.2. Monitor conditions on the pad surface and remove elevated conductance liquids and soils when discovered. I left the site at 1330 hours.

Two water puddles field tested at 19.99 mS conductance, one 6' x 1.5' x 3" deep and one 10' x 3' x 2" deep; both near the center of the north perimeter berm outfall. The water puddles were located under the freshwater and under the mixed freshwater/brine water pipelines. The puddles each had a multi-colored thin crusty film on the surface that fractured when disturbed. I collected water sample 9551-142 from the 6' x 1.5' x 3" deep puddle.I witnessed a water/muddy area in the MRC basin, pictures 8, 9 and 10, coming from the rock outfall from the center of the north side of the pad. Water in this area field tested at 16.92 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551143 from the outfall entry point into the MRC basin.Water in the MRC basin field tested at 1.595 mS conductance near the northeast MRC basin discharge. I collected sample 9551-144 from the MRC basin near the northeast discharge.The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the MRC basin.The DEP recommends the following:1. Remove the elevated conductance water puddles from the pad surface.2. Monitor conditions on the pad surface and remove elevated conductance liquids and soils when discovered. Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 08/28/2020
Comments: Site inspection at COP Tract 231 Pad A on August 28, 2020 with Rick Hall of ARD in regards to the spill reported earlier that morning. Prior to my arrival Mr. Hall was able to take some photos prior to the rain arriving. Mr. Hall's photos have been included in this inspection report. According to lease hand operator Matt Coppadge of ARD, he was manually dumping water from the dehydration unit to the produced fluids tanks via the 2" buried steel line. When Mr. Coppadge pressured back-up, he observed dust in the air and a wet spot on the surface of the well pad. He immediately stop pressurizing the line. When he assessed the well pad, he observed two holes on the surface of the well pad and a wet spot ~6-8 ft. in diameter. The release was later reported to the Department by Mr. Hall.When I arrived onsite, the well pad was wet due to the rain. Mr. Hall marked off impacted areas on the surface of the well pad based off soil screenings using a soil conductivity probe. I viewed the impacted area where the released had occurred. I screened the area using a soil probe. Soils/gravel right at the two holes on the well pad exceeded the meters range of 4.00 mS/cm. As I moved away from the holes, readings decreased. Elevated soil readings were in an area approximate 6-8 ft. in diameter. An oil sheen was observed on the well pad near the holes and in a nearby puddle of water. The contractor arrived onsite the same time I did. In addition, Matt Lock of Tuscarora Geologic & Environmental Services arrived onsite prior to my departure. Mr. Lock will be collecting samples on behalf of ARD. Please note that is 2" buried steel dump line serves all three producing Marcellus wells located on this well pad. ARD is currently unable to determine the amount of produced fluids released. Due to the unknown volume of the release, the site is required to be remediated under 78a.66 through the Act 2 process.Violations noted. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 35148

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/03/2023
Comments: On January 3, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3435475 where violations were outstanding due to a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans, and no NOV response received from the operator. Also, no production reports had been submitted since 2014 per Department database, at the time of that inspection.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photo 1). No Emergency Response plans, or other required documents were onsite. No evidence of leaks or discharge could be found around the new production tanks, and they appeared to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they were not equipped with secondary containment (see photos 3 and 8). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the earthen berms surrounding these tanks, and at the bases of these tanks (see photos 4-7). The well tag and required operator's information was present on the meter box (see photo 8). The Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite. Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 10). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing.Based on observations from today's inspection, the violations that were continued in IR 3435475 shall remain outstanding, since no changes were made since and no NOV response has been received to date. An additional violation shall be issued against the production tanks, since they are not equipped with secondary containment in an unconventional site.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted against permit 081-21855 for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from 12/19/22.

Comments: On May 17, 2022, I conducted an inspection of the Ziolkowski 11771 Well Site in Findlay Township, Allegheny County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 5/17/2022 at 12:23am. According to the report at 11:15pm, a water hauler released approximately 40 barrels of brine water to the well pad and access road. During the inspection, I observed staining along the east side of Potato Garden Road leading from the well site access road heading north toward State Route 30. I was accompanied by RRC representative Nate Smiell. The Act 9 sign was installed. The PPC plan and ER plan were on site I observed staining on the north side of the access road from the wells site entrance up to the well pad. The staining appeared to be approximately 4’ to 6’ in width, the impacted depth was estimated to be between 2" and 6" deep depending on the specific location. The Operator was in the process of scraping the stained material from the access road with a small bulldozer and loading roll off boxes with a skid steer. The Operator had progressed from the well site entrance up the access road approximately 400’. The Operator excavated the impacted material from the well pad and placed the material in roll off disposal boxes. The impacted area appeared to be approximately 480’ in length, 35’ wide with a depth of 4" to 6". The total length of the impacted area at the location (well and access road) is approximately 1,700’, with varying widths and depths. The release did not appear to reach waters of the commonwealth from the well site or access road and did not appear to impact the PCSM basins on site. The release appeared to be contained to the well pad, access road and sections the channel adjacent to the access road. Violation are being issued for the release of a regulated fluid. I recommend that the Operator continue to follow the Departments most recent spill policy for remediation of spills greater than 42 gallons.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up Inspection (FUI) of the Seneca Resources - DCNR 007 Pad K Well Site located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/5/22 @1045 hours. The weather was 70 degrees, light rain, winds S @5mph. Seneca Company Man, Travis Deleon was present onsite.During the previous inspection (IR#3376280) dated 6/10/22, a damp area and puddle was observed below the hose connection to the Highland production tank. The puddle had a field measured conductivity of 11.02 mS/cm. Sample 4427-261 was collected from the standing fluid and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for analysis. The sample results show the presence of a pollutional substance. Barium was reported at 44.78 mg/L, strontium was reported at 166.9 mg/L, and chlorides were present at 3410.8 mg/L. As of today's inspection, a small piece of secondary containment was observed installed under the hose connection on the rear side of the Highland storage tank. The area under the secondary containment was observed damp with a small amount of standing fluid. A Groline soil conductivity meter was used to measure the field conductivity of the damp soils from 1.97mS/cm - 2.37 mS/cm. A comparison of the previous photo taken of the area during the inspection on 6/10/22, to the current state of the area, indicates no pad material was removed from the impacted area. I spoke with a Seneca representative onsite and he stated production would be dispatching someone to the site to remediate the area today. A vac truck arrived onsite and removed the remaining production fluids from the Highland tank and drained the secondary containment. I again spoke with an onsite well tender regarding the removal of impacted pad material. He spoke with Jim Westbrook and stated Gas Field Specialists had been dispatched to the site and would arrive this afternoon. I completed my inspection and departed the site at 1300 hours. Gas Field Specialist personnel located me while conducting an inspection at the nearby Pad D. I informed them of the area with elevated conductivity on Pad K, where they were headed, and we discussed removal of the impacted pad material. They requested I return to the site after they had removed the impacted material to screen the area with a soil conductivity meter. None of the GFS personnel or onsite Seneca representatives possessed a conductivity meter. The impacted pad material was removed with shovels and 5 gallon buckets and placed on temporary secondary containment. I screened the excavated area for soil conductivity and found readings of less than 800 uS/cm. The area was backfilled with clean material and the secondary containment was repositioned under the hose connection. GFS personnel said they would provide the cleanup information and pictures to Seneca for followup with the DEP.Violations of the following regulations remain outstanding against API#117-22143 165HU awaiting the information requested in the NOV issued in IR#3387022 :CLS 402(b)SWMA 30125 Pa Code 78a57 control, storage and disposal of production fluids25 Pa Code 78a66(b)I again departed the site at 1530 hours.

This inspection was conducted to follow-up on the 9/17/2024 investigation into the suspected leaking pipeline that is believed to be associated with the Bickle #4 gas well. There was one open annulus vent on the wellhead and 0% combustible gas was detected at the time of inspection. Two small leaks (10% methane/volume) were detected at the fitting connecting the line to the drip and on the housing seam of the secondary meter. The violations referenced above are continuing violations. Stonehaven will be contacted to address the bubbling along the right of way and the leaks at the fittings that were identified during this inspection. No new violations cited at this time. The requested written response should include what measures have been or need to be taken to fix the leak on the pipeline associated with this well by 10/04/2024

Violation ID: 8224389
Permit API: 027-21548
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 3/11/2025
Comments: Rick Hall of EQT called at 1210 and reported an unknown amount of brine was released at the COP Tract 231 Pad A on March 11, 2025 due to a brine dump line failure.I conducted a site inspection on March 11, 2025. EQT representative Zac Subra was onsite and explained that there are 3 dump lines that run to the produced fluids tank farm. These lines are partially above and below ground (picture 2). The far left line in the picture runs from the compressor unit to the produced fluids tank farm. The other two lines run from the GPUs to the produced fluids tank farm. One is a primary main line and the other is a secondary line. According to Mr. Subra, the lease operator alternates the lines during the winter months. The lease operator discovered a leak today coming from the secondary brine line. The leak was discovered where the brine line meets gravel/soil. Standing fluids were observed in the release area with a conductivity reading of >4.00 mS/cm (picture 4). According to Mr. Subra, no fluids remain in the produced fluids tanks.EQT has contacted Tobias Machining and Welding for site remediation. Tobias staff were onsite digging potholes to try and find the buried dump lines and testing those potholes for elevated conductance. Laureen Butters of Penn E and R was onsite conducting the soil screenings. Please note, exposed soils where the release occurred and in the potholes, showed sandy soils.During my inspection several potholes were dug and tested for elevated conductance. In addition, several holes were hand dug underneath the above ground lines to help delineate the impacted area. Based off my observation a section of soils were impacted approximately 40 feet in length underneath the above ground lines. According to Mr. Subra, a vacuum truck was enroute to the site. EQT is having site meeting with production staff on the morning of March 12, 2025 to determine what production equipment can be dismantled and removed in order to proceed with site remediation. I screened along the wooded edge of the well pad adjacent to the brine spill and found no elevated conductivity readings. In addition, I screened along the edge of Million Dollar road and wooded area and found no elevated conductivity readings. Violations have been cited for the brine release. Given the unknown amount of brine released, the Department recommends that the operator pursues Act 2 for site remediation.

Comments: On November 26 2024, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection of the Mamont 16 Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued on 11/30/2021 and expires on 11/29/2026) in regards to a referral from Environmental Protection Specialist (EPS) Zane Shaffer regarding an apparent spill observed outside of secondary containment. Present during today's inspection is Zane Shaffer (DEP) and Justin Ruth (CNX). The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The Act 9 sign was present at the time of the inspection, and appeared to be in good condition. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, site plans, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS), were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of the inspection the operator was currently drilling the K well. Mr. Ruth stated the spill outside of secondary containment occurred because an empty barrel of AES WA II (SDS located in the onsite mailbox) was placed inside containment with the valve open therefore residual fluid in the barrel leaked into secondary containment. Then, pipes were accidentally placed on the side of the secondary containment causing a low spot/pinch point to form where the residual fluid mixed with rainwater was able to spill outside of the secondary containment. Mr. Ruth then stated that the pipes were removed off of the containment to stop the spill and all excess water/fluid in containment had been suctioned out.The Department then inspected the area of the apparent spill outside of secondary containment. Upon inspection, a spill was not active, however Zane Shaffer provided a picture of when the spill was active (photo 1). Upon further inspection of the spill, the Department observed orange fluid outside/underneath the secondary containment in the location where the spill had occurred. Conductivity readings were taking in the gravel/soil outside the secondary containment where the spill had occurred and obtained readings of 0.17mS and 0.13mS. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.14mS.Mr. Ruth stated that they planned to remove the matting and containment and excavate all contaminated gravel/soil and reinstall the containment once complete. He stated they hoped to have all work finished by with in a day or 2. The Department requests clarification on how much fluid was spilled/released outside of the secondary containment with in 2 days of receiving this inspection report.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed spill outside of secondary containment. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending operator response.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 12/09/2022
Comments: Routine field inspection performed in afternoon with cold, partly sunny weather conditions, and 40 degrees. Last inspection performed on 3/29/17, more than 5 years ago. Wellhead is located in soybean Agriculture field planted/harvested ~1,750' SE of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is not in close and barely visible proximity to the production facility with another well on property and shared facility. At the wellhead surface casing valve is closed, right side production tubular valve closed to port, production tubular left side valve is closed, and the production tubular plumbed on left side of head to sales/surface equipment with closed valve; annulus is exposed and vented to the atmosphere with plumbed tubular sticking out of ground and open valve union (photo #2). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is not in close, barely visible proximity to the production facility and does require a well label/marker. Some trace to occasionally moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well labeling OGA3211(H). The Department is requesting Operator add permanent well label/marker affixed at or to wellhead capturing the well details. The shared, multiple, two well (085-24005 and 085-23892) surface/ground production facility, two 50 bbl poly tanks, and two 100 bbl steel tanks all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #3). The subject well of this inspection contains surface/ground production equipment, one 50 bbl poly tank and one 100 bbl steel tank (photo #4). Valve closed on main tubular feeding separator and closed valves to and from separator (photo #5). Copper tubing lines are disconnected from production recording apparatus/chart cabinet (photos #6). A 31-day production chart is present, but not attached and without recordings dated 6/1/22 (photo #7). No production is being recorded. Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #8). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 0 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. Comments: On September 23, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Apollo Resource's Whyel 1 Well located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following violations issued under inspection report 3875658. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/25/2024 to BEAR LAKE PROP LLC in Columbus Township, Warren county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEAR LAKE PROP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/25/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8206008
Permit API: 123-39874
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Columbus Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/25/2024
Comments: The Bittinger 4 disposal injection well is housed inside a shed and is plumbed directly to the Bear Lake Properties, LLC truck unloading area located approximately 1500 feet east of the Bittinger 4 well. Multiple pieces of liner have been placed on the floor of the shed around the well. At this time, standing fluid was visible on the liner. A conductivity meter was used to find that the fluid's conductivity was greater than 20,000 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The partially exposed dirt floor at the edge of the liner was found to have soils with conductivity greater than 1,000 uS/cm, with some measurements as high as 2,500 uS/cm being observed. The fluid originating from Bittinger 4 traveled southwest from the shed to the edge of the gravel well pad, as evident from the dead vegetation and exposed soils in this direction. The portion of the gravel pad downslope of the shed was noticeably wet despite recent lack of rain. Approximately three feet southwest of the shed, a conductivity reading of 4,000 uS/cm was observed a few inches below the surface of the gravel. Approximately 70 feet southwest of the shed, soil conductivity of 2,330 uS/cm was observed in soils at the edge of the gravel pad.Background soil conductivity measurements were taken across portions of the site in areas that appeared to be unaffected by the release of fluids from Bittinger 4. Background soil conductivity readings between 200 to 300 uS/cm were observed at apparently unimpacted areas near the Bittinger 4 location.After encountering a depression at the edge of the gravel pad, the flow of the fluid was redirected southward. The southward flow was apparent via swaths of dead vegetation and bare soils that appeared to broaden in size and meander about following the terrain. This anastomosing continued for approximately 250 feet between the edge of the gravel pad to where a utility pole was located downslope of Bittinger 4. Near the utility pole, the flow of fluid again channelized and continued approximately 250 feet further down an ATV trail. At this point, as observed by dead vegetation, the majority of the released fluids crossed over the ATV trail and entered a natural drainage swale.Standing water in the drainage swale was found to have an elevated conductivity of 6,100 uS/cm. Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 4/13/2026
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 8270990
Permit API: 051-23720
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: North Union Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/13/2026
Comments: On 4/13/2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection at the Holchin 2 well plugging site in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was submitted by the operator on 3/16/2026. Tyler Hinkle (Next Level Energy) was on site during this inspection. The following was observed during the inspection:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy representative Tyler Hinkle, who was on site to make minor repairs to the temporary BMPs installed on site and to remove an excavator from site. Hinkle identified during this inspection evidence of third-party disturbance due to livestock grazing on site. The Department recommends that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. Temporary Erosion and sedimentation controls are installed downslope of the access road and well site. No evidence of accelerated erosion was observed on site during this inspection. The site E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox on site. The site appears to be staged for well plugging operations, however no machinery related to well plugging is on site at the time of inspection. The gas well is disconnected from the production equipment. No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site during this inspection. The API number was not visible anywhere on site. While on site, the Department reviewed the site E and S/Restoration plans. The Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is not installed in the location shown in the E and S plan drawing (photos 4 and 15). Although an overall BMP layout drawing exists, the plans state that E and S controls are to be installed at contractor's discretion. At the time of this inspection, the E and S controls appear to be installed on site in a manner that is preventing accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring. The Department recommends that that the operator monitor the site and install additional temporary E and S controls as necessary in order to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to occur. The Department recommends that the site E and S/Restoration plans are kept updated via redlining with the BMP's currently installed on site. Based on observations from this inspection, a violation shall be issued for failure to post the API number on site.Additional violations shall be issued in IR 4181294 for failure to follow the E and S plan.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/17/2024
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8211456
Permit API: 047-24792
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/17/2024
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone called made by Jeff Passarello, of Seneca Resources, to Brian Ayers, WQS Supervisor with the Department, on December 16, 2024. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred on Clermont Pad D. It was reported that approximately a total of 10 barrels of production fluid was released from a pipeline while doing maintenance on a pump. The pump was in secondary containment at the time of the incident. The system which controlled the flow of production fluid had not been turned off before performing maintenance on the pump. As a result, production fluid projected out of the pipeline. It is estimated that approximately 5 barrels of production fluid remained in secondary containment and approximately 5 barrels of production fluid discharged onto the well pad outside of the secondary containment. Upon arrival to the site, it was noted that the pump had been removed and placed on the pad away from where the spill occurred. The system controlling the flow of production fluid had been turned off, resolving the source of where the spill had originated. An excavator was used to remove contaminated material from the well pad. Four dumpsters were on site which contained the contaminated waste from the incident. The released production fluid appeared to be primarily within 10 yards of where the incident occurred and remained on the pad. There was no evidence of any production fluid off the well site.Confirmatory field sampling will occur to confirm full remediation of the site. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.
